requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification's view page, and the Amend action on its card in the set's notification list, open an amend confirmation page at the notification's own amend route, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants): its title and level-1 heading are 'Amend this notification?', and nothing changes until the trader confirms.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 now draws the amend confirmation as a page of its own, titled 'Amend this notification?', and the 27 November ruling sends the design's changes since 5 October to this work to catch up, which outranks the wording the 9 October afternoon ruling borrowed from the earlier pop-up (c-512). The interaction designer's 9 November answer makes amend a page in every set, plants included (c-190, c-310), and the 25 November ruling makes the view header's Amend a link to this page (c-438).
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no amend confirmation: the card's Amend is a form button that starts the amendment and opens the review page straight away (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, repo-tests-p6-001), as plants' card Amend does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-108), and the view header's 'Amend this notification' posts and starts the amendment at once (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-008, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-010).

requirements.statement: On the amend confirmation page, 'Yes, amend' is a primary button that submits the page's form (with the CSRF crumb) and starts the amendment, and 'No, cancel' is a link beside it in the button group that returns to the notification's view page without changing anything, leaving the notification Submitted; the page's Back link goes to the view page too.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place; a state change is a form post (c-189). The wording is the design's page (c-512).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, 'Cancel amend' opens the cancel-amendment confirmation as a dialog over the current page rather than sending the trader to the confirmation page, in live animals, germinal products and plants: hidden until opened, role dialog labelled by its heading, with a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; Close, the overlay and the dialog's 'Go back' dismiss it without acting and leave the trader where they were.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer is that amend and cancel amendment are their own pages, not dialogs, so the dialog increment is dropped rather than waiting on design. The design itself now draws amend as a page and keeps only cancel amendment as a dialog. GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, MoJ's modal dialog is not accepted and has no fallback without JavaScript, and no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype (c-190).

requirements.statement: Confirming an amendment ('Yes, amend' on the amend confirmation page, reached from the view page or the card's Amend) takes the trader to the notification's review page (the amend review), not to its overview hub, in every set that amends: live animals, germinal products and plants (plants' own review page).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 opens an amendment on the review page so the trader sees every answer and its Change link at once; the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps this outcome and gives plants the same landing.
requirements.deltaNote: Amend already lands on the notification's review page: the card's Amend opens it (repo-tests-p6-001, repo-tests-p6-002) and the POST to the amend address redirects there (repo-tests-p6-003). The traces of the earlier build redirected to the overview hub showing 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, trace-e2e-p14-053). Plants takes the same landing on its own review page (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-057).

requirements.statement: Amending moves a SUBMITTED notification to AMEND, keeps its reference and original submitted time, advances its concurrency token and keeps a full independent snapshot of the submitted answers, so the submitted version survives the amendment.
requirements.why: The submitted version must survive the amendment so cancelling can restore it and other services see the change.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend amend already moves SUBMITTED to AMEND, keeps submittedAt and advances the token (trace-e2e-p14-070), and the amend POST writes the snapshots (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-010); a later browser session can amend too (repo-tests-p6-004).

requirements.statement: Answers changed during an amendment are saved to the notification record (status stays AMEND) as the trader goes, and are not visible as the submitted version until resubmitted.
requirements.why: The real service persists every save; the prototype's session-only amendment cannot express persistence (c-192).
requirements.deltaNote: Every journey save advances the record's token (trace-e2e-p14-083), and a changed value survives leaving the cancel page with the amendment kept (trace-animals-fit-p3-042, repo-frontend-p7-111).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended shows the status tag 'Amend' in the shared status strip, and its card in the set's notification list reports the same status, in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the state 'Amend'; the 9 October afternoon ruling changes the shared strip's label in every set at once.
requirements.deltaNote: The strip already tags an amending notification 'Amend' (repo-tests-p6-002, repo-tests-p6-052), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-091), and the card reports it (repo-tests-p6-066). The traces of the earlier build read 'Amending' (trace-animals-fit-p3-029, trace-e2e-p14-031).

requirements.statement: During an amendment, the review page and every question page show an Amend status bar above the caption and heading: the 'Amend' tag, the reference, and a link-styled 'Cancel amend' control that goes to the cancel-amendment confirmation page. It is a change to the shared status strip, so live animals, germinal products and plants all get it at once.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader abandon the amendment from wherever they are in it; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes this the one change to the shared strip, and sends 'Cancel amend' to the confirmation page.
requirements.deltaNote: The strip already carries the Amend tag, the reference and a Cancel amend link on the overview and on every question page (repo-tests-p6-014, repo-tests-p6-015, repo-frontend-p7-122), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-098, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-099), and the review carries it as a button (repo-tests-p6-030). The traces of the earlier build offered a cancel link under the review heading alone (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-e2e-p14-055).

requirements.statement: The amend review has no page-header actions (no Amend this notification, no Copy as new), no Import reference numbers section and no Date submitted line.
requirements.why: During an amendment the status bar replaces the view page's header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's amending view shows no Copy as new or Delete under its heading (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1) and has no Import reference numbers section or Date submitted line.

requirements.statement: The amend review is editable, with a Change link on every card (the first going to the origin of the import), and its Back link goes to the notification's overview hub.
requirements.why: Amending means changing the submitted answers.
requirements.deltaNote: The amending review already has Change links on every card and a Back link to the hub (trace-e2e-p14-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-034, repo-tests-p6-061).

requirements.statement: While a submitted notification is being amended, each page the overview links to, including a question page opened from the amend review, ends with a primary 'Save and return' button that saves and goes to the amend review (which shows the changed answer), a secondary 'Save and continue' button that saves and goes to the next page, and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview' button, and no cancel link. The buttons post the service's own form fields (exit=hub and ?change=1). The party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page show 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue' only, without 'Save and return to overview'. Plants' save actions carry the same three amend controls, and its pickers the same two buttons, in the same increment.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader return to the review straight after a change, or carry on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page opened from the overview while amending ends with two buttons, 'Save and continue' then 'Save and return to overview', with a 'Cancel and return to overview' link below them that discards what was typed (repo-tests-p6-012, repo-tests-p6-013, repo-tests-p6-016); there is no 'Save and return' to the review, and a Change link's page returns to the review only by walking on with Save and continue (repo-tests-p6-017, repo-tests-p6-018, repo-tests-p6-019, trace-e2e-p14-047). The origin, CPH number and permanent address pages end with 'Save and continue' alone (repo-tests-p6-020, repo-tests-p6-021, repo-tests-p6-023). The pickers, CPH number and permanent address pages keep to two buttons because of DR1 rule (b) (document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-055, c-210), and the prototype's action field is set aside by c-267.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy, and they are the same pages a draft uses, reached at the same addresses.
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p6-017, trace-e2e-p14-046), and an amendment is walked through the same journey pages as a draft with the Amend state carried in the shared strip (repo-tests-p6-100, repo-frontend-p7-132).

requirements.statement: The amend review opens with no error summary on it. Pressing Continue while any answer is missing or invalid keeps the trader on the amend review, still tagged Amend, with a 'There is a problem' error summary whose links name each task left to finish, and does not open the Declaration. Plants' amend review refuses Continue the same way.
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid, and the trader must be told in words why Continue was refused: accessibility is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and both frontends already identify the unfinished task (c-201).
requirements.deltaNote: A refused Continue already holds the trader on the review at ?refused=1 with the 'There is a problem' summary naming the unfinished task and the Amend tag kept (repo-frontend-p7-131, repo-tests-p6-026, repo-tests-p6-027, repo-tests-p6-028), and the review opens clean (repo-tests-p6-010); plants does the same (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-102).

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.
requirements.why: An amendment is resubmitted through the same declaration as a first submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Continue on the amending review already leads to the Declaration, and ticking it resubmits (repo-tests-p6-058, repo-tests-p6-060, trace-e2e-p14-056).

requirements.statement: Resubmitting an amendment shows the ordinary 'Import notification submitted' confirmation with the notification's existing reference and no wording about an amendment; the same record becomes Submitted again, read only, with the edited answers, the set's notification list shows the amended answers, and it can be amended again.
requirements.why: An amendment replaces the submitted notification rather than creating a second one.
requirements.deltaNote: Resubmission already lands on the submitted confirmation and the notification is Submitted, read only and amendable again with the edited value (repo-tests-p6-060, repo-tests-p6-062, repo-tests-p6-063, trace-e2e-p14-057, trace-e2e-p14-057-m1). The dashboard cards' empty 'Date submitted' (trace-e2e-p14-062) is the notification list's, which drops that fact (req-1075).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's title and level-1 heading are 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?', with no caption, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for cancelling an amendment, carried onto the page by the 9 October afternoon ruling; on a page the heading is the level-1 heading, where the pop-up drew a level-2.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cancel-amend page's title and level-1 heading are 'Cancel this amendment?' (repo-frontend-p7-107, repo-tests-p6-033, trace-e2e-p14-035, trace-animals-fit-p3-036-m1), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-086); plants' page shows no caption already (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-114).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page shows no body paragraph between its heading and its buttons, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel-amendment confirmation has no description line, and the 9 October afternoon ruling carries that onto the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page says 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.' (repo-frontend-p7-108, repo-tests-p6-034, trace-e2e-p14-036), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-087).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirm button reads 'Yes, cancel amendment' and is a standard (not warning) primary button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on this button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's cancel-amend page already has a standard 'Yes, cancel amendment' button (repo-frontend-p7-109, repo-tests-p6-035, trace-animals-fit-p3-038), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-088).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's way back is a link-styled 'Go back' that returns to the notification's view (the amend review while amending; plants' check answers view) and leaves the amendment in progress, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not cancelling; as a page at today's route, it goes back where today's way back goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to notification' to the notification view, which keeps the amendment and the changed value (repo-frontend-p7-110, repo-frontend-p7-111, repo-tests-p6-037, trace-e2e-p14-039), and the same in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-097-m1).

requirements.statement: 'Cancel amend' (in the Amend status bar and beside Continue on the amend review) and the card's 'Cancel amendment' go to the cancel-amendment confirmation page at the notification's own cancel-amend route in each set, which carries only the confirmation's heading and buttons: no journey strip and no Back link.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the cancel confirmation as a separate page at today's route carrying the pop-up's wording, so the page holds what the pop-up held.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend still shows the Amend journey strip (without its own Cancel amend link) and a Back link to the notification view (repo-frontend-p7-106, repo-frontend-p7-112, repo-frontend-p7-123, repo-tests-p6-036, trace-e2e-p14-034, trace-e2e-p14-037); plants has the same page with the strip and a Back link, reached from the card, the strip and its view (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-091, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-107).

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted answers, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted and created times, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted, whose Back link goes to the set's own notification list.
requirements.why: Cancelling must leave the notification exactly as it was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancel-amend already restores the submitted answers and returns to the read-only Submitted view (repo-frontend-p7-117, repo-frontend-p7-118, repo-tests-p6-040, repo-tests-p6-043, trace-e2e-p14-045), keeping the original times (trace-e2e-p14-072-m1), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-094, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-095-m1), and Back from the restored view already opens the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-119, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-106).

requirements.statement: After an amendment is cancelled, the view page shows no success banner, and the redirect to it carries ?cancelled=1 in its address, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the view page without a message; the 9 October ruling keeps ?cancelled=1, because the prototype never decides URL shapes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view opens at ?cancelled=1 with a 'Success' banner reading 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-044, trace-animals-fit-p3-045, repo-tests-p6-040, repo-tests-p6-041): the address stays, the banner goes. Plants already redirects with a cancelled marker and shows the restored Submitted notification (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-094).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every 'overall dashboard' destination, this one included, to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page, and any other status, or a notification the session does not hold, to the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-114, repo-frontend-p7-115, repo-frontend-p7-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-093).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner, in every set that has the action; a copy started on the notification view returns there and one started on the list returns to the list.
requirements.why: A real save can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: Each controller already re-renders with 500 and the recoverable-error banner (repo-frontend-p5-069, repo-frontend-p7-100, repo-frontend-p7-121, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-080, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-116), and the copy remembers where it started (repo-frontend-p5-068). Plants' copy takes the same handling with its Copy as new (req-2055).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets (live animals and germinal products), Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy; it is started by a 'Copy as new' button that also names the notification's reference for a screen reader.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that copying is immediate and quiet.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already posts to the notification's copy address and redirects straight to the new notification's overview with no page or banner of its own (repo-frontend-p5-064, repo-frontend-p5-066, trace-e2e-p3-073, trace-e2e-p3-077, trace-animals-fit-p2-075), from a button naming the reference (repo-frontend-p5-073, repo-tests-p6-065).

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and the copy is one of the trader's own notifications, listed beside its source under its own reference.
requirements.why: Copying must never alter or merge with the notification it came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy already makes a fresh DRAFT with a new reference and leaves the source alone (repo-backend-p2-039, trace-e2e-p14-073, trace-e2e-p14-074, trace-e2e-p14-075), and both notifications stay listed under their own references (repo-frontend-p5-074, repo-frontend-p5-076, repo-tests-p6-064).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.
requirements.why: These describe the trade, not the shipment, so they usually repeat.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy keeps the origin's country code, subdivision, region flag and region code (repo-backend-p2-031), and the copy's origin task comes back Complete with the same country of origin (repo-frontend-p5-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries it over with the import details.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy clears the origin's internal reference in the notification record (repo-backend-p2-031-m1), though the copy's origin page shows it from the copied fulfilments (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks What are you importing? Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps each commodity's name, code and description only and clears its species (repo-backend-p2-032); the fulfilments payload travels as it is (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the number of animals, the number of packages or the net weight: the copy's commodity details show To do, its Animals total reads 0 and its Packages/boxes total shows no figure.
requirements.why: Counts are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's overview carries the totals (1 animal, 5 packages) and marks Commodity details Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-animals-fit-p2-077): the record clears commodity details beyond name, code and description (repo-backend-p2-032), but the fulfilments payload carries them across (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over animal identifiers (ear tags, passports and the like): the copy's Identification details show To do.
requirements.why: Identifiers belong to the animals in one shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Identification details show Complete (trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-e2e-p3-075), because the fulfilments payload is copied as it is (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, the transit port of exit, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Main import reason Complete on the copy; the 17 November ruling names the exit port 'Port of exit' everywhere, so the transit follow-up is the transit port of exit.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps the reason, purpose, destination country and port of exit (repo-backend-p2-033, repo-backend-p2-036) but clears the exit date (repo-backend-p2-038). The field the design calls the transit exit border control post takes the ruled name (ruling-sam-2026-11-17-p1-005).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the additional animal details: what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, and the storage temperature.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Additional details Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps only the certified-for answer of the additional details, clearing the unweaned animals answer and the storage temperature (repo-backend-p2-034).

requirements.statement: When copying a live-animals notification, a certified-for value the set does not offer is mapped to one it does: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value the set does not offer becomes 'Further keeping'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: which values the certified-for question offers is data, which the data dictionary specifies and reference lists supply, so a mapping drawn from the prototype's own retired option values rests on neither data owner and is not a row (c-440). A copy carries certified-for over as stored.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the roles and addresses (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, each in full as stored), the CPH number and the permanent address details.
requirements.why: Trading partners usually repeat between shipments.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps the CPH number and the whole fulfilments payload (repo-backend-p2-036, repo-backend-p2-037), but keeps each party with only its name, email, phone and address (repo-backend-p2-035), so anything else stored on a party is not carried; the copy's overview shows Roles and addresses Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the arrival details (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference): the copy's Arrival details show To do.
requirements.why: Arrival is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Arrival details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109), though the backend copy clears the transport details in the record (repo-backend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transit countries.
requirements.why: The route is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transit countries show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transporter: the copy's Transport details show To do.
requirements.why: The transporter is chosen per shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transport details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the contact address: the copy's Contact address shows To do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for the contact address again on each notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Contact address shows Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-077).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over uploaded documents: the copy's Upload documents shows To do.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Upload documents already shows To do on a copy (trace-e2e-p3-076, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copies the saved notification; an unfinished amendment is not yet the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today copying an AMEND notification copies its current, in-progress answers rather than the amendment snapshot (repo-backend-p2-039-m1).

requirements.statement: Copy as new for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, a notification with no content, or a status that cannot be copied such as deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that copies.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already returns a refused copy to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p5-067); the backend refuses a source with no content (repo-backend-p2-040), and plants' backend refuses an uncopyable status (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-023).

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: when the notification has changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started, the set's notification list or the notification's view page, with the 'The notification has been updated' banner, in live animals, germinal products and plants.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits. The 25 November ruling gives plants the same stale-copy return now that its header offers Copy as new.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p5-070, repo-frontend-p5-072, trace-e2e-p14-073, repo-tests-p6-054, repo-tests-p6-055), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves, so the trader lands on a page that does not exist (repo-frontend-p5-071). Plants' persistence already posts the token with its copy (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-024).

requirements.statement: The amend review ends with a button group of 'Continue', a secondary 'Cancel amend' and a warning-styled 'Delete' that opens the notification's delete confirmation page, in every set that amends, and a notification being amended is deleted as any other notification is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete during an amendment at the foot of the amend review.
requirements.deltaNote: Both frontends already delete a notification being amended (repo-frontend-p7-094, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-075), and the amending card offers Delete (trace-e2e-p14-060), but the live animals amending view offers no Delete (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1), plants' amending view ends with Continue, Cancel amend and Save and return to overview and no Delete (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-100), and nothing proves deleting an amending notification (repo-frontend-p5-078, trace-animals-fit-p3-057).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin), in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same layout in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p7-086, repo-frontend-p7-089), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-069, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070), where the reference and status come from the journey strip instead (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-074).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, the Commodity row on the delete and amend confirmation pages lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, the commodity lines comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis aries), Goat (Capra hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's format for naming what was notified, the same on both confirmation pages. Whether the Latin names are re-cased is its own question (c-510).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the Number row on the delete and amend confirmation pages shows the notification's total number of animals across all its commodity lines.
requirements.why: Animals are counted by head. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement by set; the germinal set's packages count is its own requirement.

requirements.statement: A summary row on the delete or amend confirmation page that has no value from the notification shows 'Not applicable', in every set.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft. The design's fall-back to its own list's seeded details exists for its demo data, which the real service, whose list reads the same record, does not have.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page has no such sentence (repo-frontend-p7-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's warning wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'This cannot be undone.' (repo-frontend-p7-089, trace-e2e-p3-060), in plants too, in a plain paragraph (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070).

requirements.statement: The delete page's red warning button reads 'Yes, delete', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p7-090, repo-tests-p6-047, trace-animals-fit-p3-008), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' that leaves the notification in place (repo-frontend-p7-091, repo-frontend-p7-092, trace-animals-fit-p3-009), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-079).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page, in every set (plants' check answers view).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader back to the notification they were deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-093, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-072).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading and offers no Cancel amend control, in every set; the summary list identifies the notification instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds the page from GOV.UK components only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page shows the journey strip with the status tag and reference (trace-animals-fit-p3-011, trace-animals-fit-p3-012, trace-e2e-p3-064), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-074).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', is reached from the Delete action on the notification's card in the set's list and from the notification's view, serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's delete page already has this title and heading for drafts and submitted notifications (repo-frontend-p7-088, repo-tests-p6-046, trace-animals-fit-p3-006-m1, trace-animals-fit-p3-013), reached from each card's Delete (repo-frontend-p7-087, repo-tests-p6-050) and the view's Delete (repo-tests-p6-053, trace-e2e-p13-110) at /notifications/{id}/delete (repo-frontend-p7-086, trace-e2e-p3-065), and plants' delete page is the same (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-066, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-069).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; deleting a submitted notification records a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event carrying the acting user's organisation id; a notification the trader's session does not hold is not deleted. Plants soft-deletes through its own backend the same way.
requirements.why: The real store keeps deleted records for other services and audit; the prototype's outright removal cannot express persistence (c-193).
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes, idempotently (repo-frontend-p7-097, repo-tests-p6-051, trace-e2e-p14-077, trace-e2e-p14-078), for a submitted notification carrying address-book parties as for a draft, with the organisation id forwarded for the event (repo-frontend-p7-099, trace-animals-fit-p3-024), refuses a notification the session does not hold (repo-frontend-p7-098, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-076), and plants keeps the record and marks it deleted (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the set's own notification list (the live-animals set root, the germinal products set root, plants' own list), and the redirect keeps ?deleted=1 in its address.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sends every Design Release 2.1 'overall dashboard' destination, the delete landing included, to the set's own list, replacing the INS landing; the 9 October ruling keeps ?deleted=1 on the redirect (c-198, c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals delete already lands on /live-animals?deleted=1 (repo-frontend-p7-096, repo-tests-p6-051, trace-e2e-p3-066), and plants' on its own list with a deleted marker (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077); the germinal set gets it with its copy of the feature.

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads 'Notification has been deleted.' in the live animals and plants lists.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for a list that does not know the deleted notification's reference: its '<reference> has been deleted.' form needs the reference, and the 9 October ruling keeps the redirect's address as ?deleted=1, which does not carry it (c-513). The germinal products list's message is its own question (c-511).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner is titled 'Notification deleted' and reads 'The notification has been deleted.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-017, trace-animals-fit-p3-018, repo-tests-p6-048, trace-e2e-p3-068), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-078). The banner's 'Success' title is req-1086's.

requirements.statement: A deleted notification does not appear in the set's notification list, and searching the list for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, repo-tests-p6-049, trace-e2e-p3-072), and from plants' list (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, another session's notification, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends the guard to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p7-095, repo-frontend-p7-098), as plants' does on both opening and confirming (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-076).

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same numbered sections and cards as the review page; the sections and the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences in the sections and inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads the source at the caller's concurrency token and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend already implements this lifecycle, proven through the API (trace-e2e-p14-064, trace-e2e-p14-067, trace-e2e-p14-070, trace-e2e-p14-072, trace-e2e-p14-073, trace-e2e-p14-077, trace-e2e-p14-067-m1) and modelled as four statuses by the suite (repo-tests-p6-052).

requirements.statement: A notification is saved as a draft as the trader goes: one record per reference, keeping its created date, without errors or transient page state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 autosaves drafts; the real service persists each save.
requirements.deltaNote: Each journey page's save already persists the whole record under its reference (trace-e2e-p14-083).

requirements.statement: The delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the restored submitted view and a copied notification's overview have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: The service must meet accessibility standards.
requirements.deltaNote: The fit specs already assert this (repo-frontend-p5-077, repo-frontend-p7-103, repo-frontend-p7-128, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-081, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-096).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's animals specs and page objects for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the copy, the confirmation pages (the amend confirmation page included), the landing pages and the banners these requirements give, assert ?cancelled=1 on the cancel redirect and ?deleted=1 on the delete redirect, keep the smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases, and cover the delete page's body copy and its way back, the cancel page's way-back wording, deleting a notification that is being amended, the guard redirects, a stale amend review, what cancelling does to a document added during the amendment, and what a deleted notification's own view shows.
requirements.why: End-to-end proof must follow the changed behaviour, and the gaps the suite leaves today are the cases these requirements change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's specs assert the current copy ('Yes, delete notification', 'Cancel this amendment?', its body paragraph, the cancel alert, ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1) (repo-tests-p6-033, repo-tests-p6-034, repo-tests-p6-047, repo-tests-p6-048), expect Amend to open the review straight away (repo-tests-p6-001), name no delete-page body copy or way back (repo-tests-p6-107), do not pin the cancel page's way-back wording (repo-tests-p6-108), and prove nothing about a stale amend review, a document added during an amendment or a deleted notification's own view (repo-tests-p6-109, repo-tests-p6-110, repo-tests-p6-111).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the amend confirmation page and the view page has a Welsh entry of the same shape, and the copy tests that pin those strings verbatim are updated with them, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: Today's action pages carry Welsh copy, and the frontend's standing rule (req-1659) is that every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version of the same shape; Design Release 2.1 is silent on Welsh, so nothing it shows overrides that rule.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete and cancel-amend pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy carrying exactly the English keys (repo-frontend-p7-105, repo-frontend-p7-130), and plants' copies of them too, with its delete strings pinned verbatim by their own test (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-083, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-110).

requirements.statement: Delete and cancel amendment are checked against the version the trader opened, and the dashboard Amend carries a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: delete and cancel-amend post a token nobody reads, and Amend posts none. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for a fix, so the programme does not make one.

requirements.statement: Soft delete checks that the caller owns the notification or is an admin.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as an access-control weakness in the backend: its lifecycle calls carry only the API key and no caller identity. Design Release 2.1 does not cover it, so it needs its own ticket.

requirements.statement: Create, save, copy, submit, amend and cancel-amend write audit records attributed to a user.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: the backend's lifecycle calls take no body and no user id, so nothing attributes them. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for audit.

requirements.statement: Backend edge cases answer with a client error rather than a server error: copy of a source with no content, and submit of an empty notification.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as backend defects no user journey reaches; Design Release 2.1 does not cover them.

requirements.statement: The place of destination picker's search does not fail with HTTP 500, and the 500 page offers a way back.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: seen on the copy test's first attempt, it belongs to the address pickers and the error page, not to copying.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics are reproduced: its session keys and journey resets, the ?resume=1 shortcut into an amendment, ?reference addressing, a default reference, deleted-reference lists, seeded review snapshots and their fixed sample data, the confirmation summary's fall-back to the list's seeded details, and its seed-format arrival answers.
requirements.why: Prototype internals with nothing a user sees; the real service persists notifications in the backend, holds one record per notification and has its own test data.

requirements.statement: Amend for a notification the trader cannot amend (unknown reference, a notification since deleted, or any status but Submitted, such as Draft or one already being amended) changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends, both on opening the amend confirmation page and on confirming it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the amend route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list, plants' included.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amend pressed on a card for a notification since deleted lands on the set's list with an Important banner reading 'This notification could not be amended.' (repo-tests-p6-005, repo-tests-p6-006): the landing stays, the banner goes.

requirements.statement: The k6 amendment journey in the performance-test suite checks that Amend lands on the notification's amend review; it edits the origin page, then either cancels at cancel-amend, landing on the view page with cancelled=1, or resubmits through the review and the declaration.
requirements.why: Amend moving to the amend review breaks the k6 'amendment started' check, which expects the hub; the suite changes in the amend increment because that increment breaks one of its scripts (ruling 2026-10-07, c-225), and cancel-amend keeps its route and ?cancelled=1.
requirements.deltaNote: The k6 amend step still posts the crumb to <base>/amend and checks it lands on the hub at <base>, while the frontend already redirects to the notification's review page (repo-tests-p6-002, repo-tests-p6-003) and cancel-amend to the view with ?cancelled=1 (repo-tests-p6-045).

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the Number row on the delete and amend confirmation pages shows the notification's total quantity (units or pieces) across its lines.
requirements.why: Germinal products are counted by their quantity in units or pieces, the line's mandatory count, not by head (c-234); Design Release 2.1's Number row shows the germinal total quantity. The 9 October ruling splits req-1444 into a live half and a germinal half, and keeps the germinal content for the germinal set's copies.

requirements.statement: A copy of a germinal products notification keeps the certified-for answer 'Germinal products'; it is never mapped to 'Further keeping' as an outdated live-animals value would be.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the mapping of outdated certified-for values it guards against is not built, because which values the question offers is data the dictionary and the reference lists own rather than the prototype (c-440). A copy carries certified-for over as stored (req-1429), so the germinal answer survives with no rule of its own.

requirements.statement: A copy keeps its source's category: copying a germinal products notification makes a germinal products draft (still a GBN-AG reference) that only the germinal set opens, and copying a live-animals notification makes a live-animals draft.
requirements.why: The backend stores the category on the record and each set opens only its own category, so a copy that lost its category would open in the wrong set or not at all.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend builds a copy as a fresh notification from the source's answers (repo-backend-p2-039), and nothing in what it carries is the category.

requirements.statement: After a delete, the set's own notification list it lands on at ?deleted=1 shows the deletion success message at once, in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants); opening the list again without ?deleted=1 shows no deletion message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the message on the live-animals list; the 9 October afternoon ruling lands the delete there, and the 9 October ruling drops the session flash, so the message travels only with ?deleted=1 (c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals list already shows the banner at ?deleted=1 and none on a plain reload (repo-frontend-p7-096, trace-e2e-p3-070-m1), and plants' list shows it at its deleted marker (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-078); the germinal list copies the live animals list as it is on main (ruling-sam-2026-11-27-p1-022).

requirements.statement: The deletion success banner stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page, in every set.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen-reader or slow reader has it (WCAG 2.2.1); the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps success banners on screen, so Design Release 2.1's 5-second dismissal is not built (c-271).
requirements.deltaNote: Today's deletion banner is a standard GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert that stays on the page (trace-animals-fit-p3-019, trace-e2e-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The delete and amend journeys take the earlier parity programme's changes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: that programme had neither journey at its root and its dashboard card offered only Copy as new and View; row inc-026's own verifier found that no frontend work follows under either reading of its scope question, and Design Release 2.1 is the comparison these journeys are built to (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p3-022, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p3-057).

requirements.statement: Plants' notification view header offers 'Copy as new' in a form of its own beside 'Amend this notification' and 'Delete', so the plants and live animals headers offer the same three actions.
requirements.why: The 25 November ruling gives the plants header a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions, answering the question the other way from its default (c-447).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the plants view header offers only Amend and Delete (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-027).

requirements.statement: In plants, the summary list rows ('Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number', 'Origin') on the delete and amend confirmation pages are filled from plants' own notification: its reference, its commodity as plants names it, its quantity, and its country of origin.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling mirrors the delete page into plants in the same increment, keeping plants' own data, and the amend confirmation page carries the same rows.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' delete page today has only its heading, one sentence and two buttons, with the reference carried by the journey strip (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-069, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-074), and plants has no amend confirmation page.

requirements.statement: The plants frontend's own fit specs for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the changed pages: the amend confirmation page; the delete page's summary, wording, 'Yes, delete', 'No, cancel' and Back link to the view page; the cancel-amendment page's heading, its absent body paragraph and 'Go back'; and Copy as new from the view header landing on the new draft. They assert the deleted and cancelled markers, the restored Submitted notification and no serious or critical axe violations, and cover deleting a submitted or amending notification and the cancel page's redirect for a notification that is not being amended.
requirements.why: Plants' fit specs prove its pages today and must follow them in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' specs assert 'No, return to dashboard' and a Back link to the list on delete, and 'Cancel this amendment?' with its body paragraph on cancel, with the delete strings pinned verbatim by their own test (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-079, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-072, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-086, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-082); Amend starts from the card with no confirmation (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-108); the guard redirects are proven by controller tests rather than fit specs (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-092).

requirements.statement: In plants, Copy as new on the notification view header makes a new plants draft with its own reference, leaving the source unchanged, carrying exactly what plants' existing copy carries of its own answers, and takes the trader straight to the new draft's overview with no confirmation and no banner; a refused, stale or failed copy is handled as in live animals.
requirements.why: The 25 November ruling builds Copy as new for plants too. Every layer beneath the button is already on plants' main (its backend copy and copy mapper, its real and stub persistence, its engine's copyJourney), so it is wiring rather than a feature build and the plants backend does not change; what the copy carries is therefore what that existing copy gives plants' own fields, and the landing and handling mirror live animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' backend copy, its persistence and its engine's copyJourney already exist (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-021, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-024, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-026); only the header action and its route are missing (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-028).

requirements.statement: Plants settles its parked post-submission policy: whether an amended arrival date re-runs the late timing test, whether a first-submission timestamp is kept, and whether a notification the regulator has acted on may be amended or withdrawn.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: plants parked these as policy questions, and Design Release 2.1 does not answer them; meanwhile cancelling an amendment keeps the original submission instant, so the late flag stays frozen at first submission.

requirements.statement: While a plants notification is being amended, its question pages end with the same three amend controls as live animals ('Save and return' to the review page, a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview'), and its address pickers with the same two buttons ('Save and return' and 'Save and continue'). The controls use plants' own form fields (exit=hub, ?change=1).
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling makes inc-004 (page endings while amending, req-1624 and req-1403) change plants in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' pages end the same whether or not the notification is being amended: the commodities list page offers 'Save and continue' alone (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-103), and a question page's way out of the overview is a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that saves nothing (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-104). Plants amends a submitted notification from its dashboard card (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-108).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a 'Submitted action required' notification can be amended, copied and deleted as a Submitted one can: 'Amend this notification' and the amend confirmation start its amendment, cancelling that amendment restores it to 'Submitted action required' with its submitted answers, Copy as new copies it into a new draft, and Delete soft-deletes it. Resubmitting the amendment records the status the outstanding items give at that moment.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 16 November ruling withdraws the 'Submitted action required' status, so a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other and already takes every one of these actions; nothing action-required is shown until the banner design is agreed (c-439).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, a completed notification, tagged 'Past', can be copied (Copy as new makes a new draft from it) and deleted (soft delete, with a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event), but not amended: its view offers no Amend, and amend for it is refused like any other status that cannot be amended.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Copy as new and Delete, and no Amend, on a completed ('Past') notification. The 16 November ruling holds the completed status out until a real source of completion exists, and it arrives only once the authorities' outcomes reach the service, so the actions wait with it.
requirements.deltaNote: No completed status exists today: the suite models four statuses (repo-tests-p6-052), and delete accepts only draft, submitted and amending notifications (repo-frontend-p7-094). Design Release 2.1 does not trace copying or deleting a completed notification (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p16-102). Whether plants takes the status is decided when it unblocks (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-065).
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion must reach the notification record: the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sending post-submission outcomes, including completed, as req-1082 waits on. The 16 November ruling holds the status out until one exists (ruling-sam-2026-11-16-p1-017).

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, 'Save and return', 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make exactly the same checks on the page's answers, on every page that offers them, in live animals, germinal products and plants: with any answer missing or not valid the trader stays on the page and sees an error message for each one, with what they entered still in the fields; with every answer given and valid, the button saves and goes where its own wording says. No page is an exception: on the CPH number, permanent address, contact address and plants consignment contact pages each of these buttons checks whatever the page needs before the trader moves on, and on upload documents a part-filled document is refused by every one of them, with an error for each missing detail, while a complete document is saved and kept.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling makes the save buttons behave the same as each other, so a trader who leaves a page by any of them is told what is missing or wrong instead of carrying an unchecked answer into the overview, and documents behave like every other page; the 27 November ruling keeps that default in live animals, the germinal products copy and plants' pages alike. The CPH number, permanent address and contact address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, take the same rule: what each of them needs before the trader moves on is unchanged, and every save control checks it alike.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and return to overview' while amending accepts a cleared mandatory answer and lands on the overview with no error, so the missing answer is reported only later on the review (repo-tests-p6-026), and the page's way out that discards an answer is a 'Cancel and return to overview' link (repo-tests-p6-013, repo-tests-p6-016). The 'Save and return' control itself does not exist yet (trace-e2e-p14-047), so its checks are built with it (req-1403, req-2068).

requirements.statement: An amendment keeps a copy of the notification's answers as they were when it started and compares the trader's answers with that copy, counting the notification as changed when they differ and never changed when no copy was taken, ignoring everything that is not an answer (errors, messages, the commodity search box, the status, the amend bookkeeping, version flags, drafts, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted references and address book additions).
requirements.why: Out of scope: this is the prototype's own session bookkeeping, and the prototype's source does not say what any page does with the result (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-084). The real service already holds the submitted answers as the amend snapshot and answers the same question with a yes-or-no value of its own (req-2366), so there is nothing of the prototype's comparison for the programme to build.

requirements.statement: Once the trader has saved an answer that differs from the submitted one during an amendment, the amend review's title and level-1 heading read 'Review before re-submitting'; until then they read 'Review your notification', in live animals, germinal products and plants.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the page for what the trader is about to do, so the heading tells the trader an amendment is waiting to be re-submitted rather than simply reviewed; the service holds a yes-or-no 'answers differ from submitted' value that says when it has happened (c-371).
requirements.deltaNote: Live animals already switches the heading once an answer has changed and keeps 'Review your notification' until then (repo-tests-p6-007, repo-tests-p6-008, repo-tests-p6-011, repo-frontend-p7-111); the trace of the earlier build kept one heading throughout (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-051), and no claim shows plants' view taking the second heading, so plants takes it with this requirement.

requirements.statement: A rulings or decisions ledger in the animals set's four end-of-notification feature folders.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: the recorded-decisions-animals area weighs whether the animals frontend keeps a decisions ledger and where.

requirements.statement: The animals backend records whether the answers of a notification being amended differ from the submitted ones as a yes-or-no value that is never empty, and the animals frontend reads that value from the backend's shape, in its local stub as against the real service, rather than working it out itself.
